lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Real-time analytics Data warehousing Observability AI-powered application features such as generated insights, anomaly detection, recommendations, and natural language interfaces to product data, all require a tight feedback loop between transactional writes and analytical reads.

claims.text: Real-time analytics Data warehousing Observability AI-powered application features such as generated insights, anomaly detection, recommendations, and natural language interfaces to product data, all require a tight feedback loop between transactional writes and analytical reads.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: The standard architecture for this is Postgres + ClickHouse: Postgres handles transactions and application state, ClickHouse handles analytics.

claims.text: The standard architecture for this is Postgres + ClickHouse: Postgres handles transactions and application state, ClickHouse handles analytics.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: ClickHouse provides fast ingestion, sub-second queries on billions of rows, and the concurrency levels that customer-facing applications require.

claims.text: ClickHouse provides fast ingestion, sub-second queries on billions of rows, and the concurrency levels that customer-facing applications require.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: As applications become agentic, this pairing becomes more critical.

claims.text: As applications become agentic, this pairing becomes more critical.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Postgres + ClickHouse: Postgres handles transactions and application state, ClickHouse handles analytics.

claims.text: Postgres + ClickHouse: Postgres handles transactions and application state, ClickHouse handles analytics.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Agents must query live product data continuously, which increases both query frequency and concurrency.

claims.text: Agents must query live product data continuously, which increases both query frequency and concurrency.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Natural language analytics interfaces (sometimes called AI Analyst) are moving from experimentation into production.

claims.text: Natural language analytics interfaces (sometimes called AI Analyst) are moving from experimentation into production.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Users ask questions in plain English and expect answers in seconds.

claims.text: Users ask questions in plain English and expect answers in seconds.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: The infrastructure implication is that a single natural language query does not generate one SQL query — it typically generates dozens in rapid succession as the agent explores available datasets and evaluates multiple reasoning paths.

claims.text: The infrastructure implication is that a single natural language query does not generate one SQL query — it typically generates dozens in rapid succession as the agent explores available datasets and evaluates multiple reasoning paths.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: As a result, internal analyst workloads start to resemble external customer-facing workloads in their concurrency and latency profile.

claims.text: As a result, internal analyst workloads start to resemble external customer-facing workloads in their concurrency and latency profile.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: ClickHouse addresses this with a native Postgres + ClickHouse integration that provides automatic data replication and a unified developer experience, removing the need to manage a separate CDC pipeline.

claims.text: ClickHouse addresses this with a native Postgres + ClickHouse integration that provides automatic data replication and a unified developer experience, removing the need to manage a separate CDC pipeline.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Full-fidelity events are stored once, and metrics, traces, and SLOs are derived from them at query time rather than pre-aggregated on ingest.

claims.text: Full-fidelity events are stored once, and metrics, traces, and SLOs are derived from them at query time rather than pre-aggregated on ingest.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: ClickHouse is well-suited for this model: High compression on log and event data Sub-second queries on high-cardinality wide events Efficient ingestion at production infrastructure volumes Cost model based on compute and storage, not per-GB ingestion fees ClickStack is ClickHouse’s observability stack built on this model, using OpenTelemetry as the data collection layer.

claims.text: ClickHouse is well-suited for this model: High compression on log and event data Sub-second queries on high-cardinality wide events Efficient ingestion at production infrastructure volumes Cost model based on compute and storage, not per-GB ingestion fees ClickStack is ClickHouse’s observability stack built on this model, using OpenTelemetry as the data collection layer.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Legacy data warehouses were designed for infrequent, batch-oriented queries.

claims.text: Legacy data warehouses were designed for infrequent, batch-oriented queries.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: They optimize for overall throughput across many queries, not for sub-second response times at high concurrency.

claims.text: They optimize for overall throughput across many queries, not for sub-second response times at high concurrency.

lines.text: And at the data level, the same events are often stored twice — once in an observability platform and once in a data warehouse — with a fragile synchronization layer in between.

claims.text: And at the data level, the same events are often stored twice — once in an observability platform and once in a data warehouse — with a fragile synchronization layer in between.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: Storing all of it once in open formats, queryable by both AI Analyst and AI SRE tooling, removes that duplication and makes context available across both workflows.

claims.text: Storing all of it once in open formats, queryable by both AI Analyst and AI SRE tooling, removes that duplication and makes context available across both workflows.

lines.text: Data warehousing and observability have historically been separate domains with separate vendors, buyers, and stacks.

claims.text: Data warehousing and observability have historically been separate domains with separate vendors, buyers, and stacks.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.text: That separation is increasingly a convention rather than a technical requirement.

lines.text: Both domains now write to object storage.
